F i g u r e 9.21 A gas mol­e­cule follows a straight-line path for only a short time before undergoing a collision, so its overall path is a zigzag one. The displacement Dr of a particular mol­e­cule in time, Dt, is shown. The path taken by the molecules is traced out in blue, and the red arrow represents the net displacement during the period Dt. The mean- square displacement Dr 2 is equal to 6Dt, where D is the diffusion constant of the mol­e­cules in the gas.

The mean free path, unlike the collision frequency, does not depend on the molar mass. The mean free path must be much larger than the mo­lec­u­lar diameter for a gas to show ideal gas behavior. For a mol­e­cule of diameter 3 × 10210 m, the mean free path at 25°C and atmospheric pressure is 1 × 1027 m, which is 300 times larger.
